domain_label: Movie Studio — Persona Bible Design for Two Fictional Classic-Luxurious Personas (1 M + 1 F)
purpose: A method for the units of expert work in designing and governing the persona bibles of two fictional classic-luxurious personas (one male, one female): the fixed verbatim descriptor block and its two hard rules, the descriptor-axis vocabulary generators actually respect (age, face geometry, eyes, skin, hair, build, marks), backstory-as-prompt-anchor and its honest division of labor against reference conditioning, the worked A/B bibles held as owner-sign-off proposals, per-persona color palettes and accessory continuity sets, grooming-state enumeration and versioned bible changes, duo staging conventions and their Higgsfield routing under the one-soul-per-generation constraint, and the batch QC gate — with the likeness closed-lane kept closed (both personas fictional, resembling no specific real person) and every platform capability quoted only from the live-surface enumeration.
assumptions: no generation batches have been run yet; every score is a heuristic prior and every drift/fidelity magnitude flagged [UNKNOWN] in the grounding research stays unknown until the run phase

all Higgsfield model ids, parameters, constraints and media roles are quoted from the live MCP surface enumeration of 2026-07-03 (higgsfield_surface.md), never from memory: soul_2/soul_cinematic take an optional soul_id with ONE soul_id per generation; soul_cast is text-only 16:9 with budget 10-500; Elements are instant references embedded as <<<element_id>>> placeholders with categories character|environment|prop and are not usable with the Soul models; Souls train from 5-20 images in ~10 min

the 50-100 word bible band and the descriptor-axis effectiveness claims are practitioner consensus from consistency guides (sources 22-23 of the grounding file), carried as [FACT] on the fixed-verbatim-block principle and [ESTIMATE] on the exact word band and axis synthesis

the worked persona-A and persona-B bible texts, palettes, grooming proposals and duo grammar are authored [ESTIMATE] proposals awaiting owner sign-off — appearance decisions belong to the owner, so no bible text here is final canon
both personas are fictional composites of categorical descriptors; no descriptor set is derived from, or audited against only, a single real individual
exclusions: wardrobe module construction, capsule theory, formality bands and the outfit-combination grammar beyond the per-persona palette and accessory continuity set (that system is the wardrobe KB's work)
drift-detection engineering detail (embedding model choice, FAR/FRR math) and the anti-AI realism QC gates beyond the persona-level checklist and the calibrate-empirically mandate
video pipeline mechanics (start/end-frame chaining, clip stitching, motion control) beyond naming which identity carrier a duo or solo frame routes through
any guidance for evoking a specific real person while hiding or obscuring the face — the likeness closed lane stays closed and this KB refuses that work rather than scoping it
invented engagement statistics, platform policies, legal cases or psychology effect sizes — nothing beyond what the grounding files carry, at the tags they carry

glossary.definition: A fixed, canonical descriptor block pasted verbatim into every prompt — roughly 50-100 words covering age, build, hair, face, eyes, outfit, signature item [FACT on the fixed-verbatim principle, sources 22-23; the exact word band is practitioner consensus held [ESTIMATE]]. Too short and the model fills gaps differently each time; too long and parts get ignored.

Bible hard rule 1: 'shoulder-length dark brown hair' must never become 'brunette' — generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens, so any paraphrase re-rolls the attribute [FACT — consistency-guide corpus, sources 22-23].
Bible hard rule 2: keep the character block at the very start of the prompt; shifting its position changes the weight the model assigns to it [FACT — same corpus].

A coarse, high-signal categorical attribute a generator actually responds to (face shape, jawline, eye color + shape, skin tone + undertone, hair slots, somatotype build), as opposed to millimetre geometry it cannot hold [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the guide corpus, medium-high confidence].

The rule that hair is always specified as length + texture + specific color + style/part side + finish (e.g. 'collarbone-length, softly waved, dark espresso brown, centre-parted, natural sheen') and no slot is ever dropped — dropped slots are re-sampled and read as drift [ESTIMATE — authored craft from the guide corpus].

A 1-2 line persona context line ('A 34-year-old European heir who splits time between a Lake Como villa and a Mayfair townhouse; understated, athletic, never hurried') that steers the model's default fills for wardrobe, posture, setting and grading, and keeps human prompt-authors consistent — while stabilizing nothing about face geometry [ESTIMATE — mechanism inference, high confidence on the division of labor].

A single mole/freckle pattern written into the bible so a human QC pass can spot drift; generators frequently drop or migrate marks, so the mark is a drift TEST SIGNAL for rejecting shots, never a reliability guarantee of identity [ESTIMATE — widely reported in consistency guides, medium confidence].

The per-persona color set every wardrobe and accessory choice must draw from (A: navy/charcoal/camel/ivory/forest green, brushed steel or white gold, dark brown leather; B: ivory/cream/champagne/camel/black/powder blue, yellow gold or pearl, tan leather) — authored [ESTIMATE] proposals aligned with quiet-luxury palette guidance, awaiting owner sign-off.

On the live Higgsfield surface: a Soul is a trained identity model (5-20 images, ~10 min) usable only with soul_2/soul_cinematic and only ONE soul_id per generation; an Element is an instant no-training reference embedded as <<<element_id>>> placeholders (categories character|environment|prop), multiple per prompt, not usable with the Soul models [FACT — higgsfield_surface.md, live MCP surface 2026-07-03]. Whether Elements lose identity fidelity vs Souls is [UNKNOWN].

The refused request class: evoking a specific real person while hiding or obscuring the face. Both personas are fictional composites resembling no specific real person; the lane stays closed with no workaround guidance, and reference fashion houses are aesthetic reference only, never claimed brand identity.

nodes.definition: Establish the anchor artifact of the whole domain: the character bible is a fixed, canonical descriptor block pasted verbatim into every prompt. Community-converged guidance across consistency guides puts it at roughly 50-100 words covering age, build, hair, face, eyes, outfit and a signature item — too short and the model fills the gaps differently each time; too long and parts get ignored [FACT that this is the converged guidance, sources 22-23; the exact word band is practitioner consensus held [ESTIMATE], with high confidence on the fixed-verbatim-block principle itself]. Two hard rules govern its use [FACT — same corpus]: (1) identical phrasing forever — 'shoulder-length dark brown hair' must never become 'brunette', because generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens; (2) fixed token position — the block sits at the very start of the prompt, because shifting its position changes the weight the model assigns to it. Every other node in this KB either fills this block or governs how it changes.

the identical-phrasing and fixed-token-position hard rules

excluded: which descriptor axes go inside it (its own node)

pros.claim: A verbatim block turns persona identity text into a controlled constant across hundreds of generations instead of a per-prompt improvisation
pros.example: pasting the same 70-word block into shot 1 and shot 400 so wardrobe, age and grooming read as the same person even months apart

cons.claim: The 50-100 word budget caps how many axes the block can carry, forcing prioritization and pushing overflow into modules and references
cons.example: a block that tries to carry all eight wardrobe modules blows past 100 words and the generator starts ignoring the face lines

failure_modes: paraphrasing the block per shot so synonyms re-roll attributes
moving the block mid-prompt and silently changing its weight
letting the block grow past the band until parts get ignored

nodes.definition: Fix the boundary the whole program lives inside: both personas are FICTIONAL people assembled from categorical descriptors, resembling no specific real person. Three binding rules. (1) Closed lane: any request to evoke a specific real person while hiding or obscuring the face is refused — no descriptor recipe, no 'inspired by' workaround, no partial-face trick; this KB scopes the refusal, not the technique. (2) Composite audit: because precise descriptor stacks can accidentally converge on a recognizable individual, the rendered persona sheets are audited against the question 'does this read as a specific real person?' and descriptors are adjusted whenever the answer is yes. (3) Brand likeness: quiet-luxury reference houses named in the research (Loro Piana, Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna, The Row, Savile Row tailors) are aesthetic reference ONLY — generated content never claims or depicts brand identity [FACT that these are the genre's named reference brands, sources 29-31 of the grounding file; the never-depict rule is the program's own binding policy]. Note also the platform-adjacent fact that reference tools are weaker on real faces anyway: Midjourney's own doc says images of real people 'typically won't look exactly like them' [FACT — search excerpt of official doc, direct fetch 403-blocked].

included: the fictional-composite requirement for both personas
the refused closed lane (specific real person, hidden face)
the composite-convergence audit and brands-as-aesthetic-reference-only rule
excluded: legal analysis of likeness rights (no legal cases are carried in the grounding research)

pros.claim: A hard fictionality guardrail lets hundreds of generations proceed without per-shot legal or ethical re-litigation
pros.example: clearing a 200-shot batch because the personas were audited as fictional composites once, at design time, instead of reviewing each frame for accidental celebrity likeness from scratch

cons.claim: The audit is a human judgment call with no quantitative test in the grounding research, so borderline convergence cases need conservative rejection
cons.example: a persona sheet that several reviewers 'almost recognize' must be re-composited even though no metric flagged it

answering a hidden-face evocation request with technique instead of refusal

nodes.definition: Fix the granularity at which the bible speaks: generators respond to coarse, high-signal CATEGORICAL attributes, not millimetre geometry [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the consistency-guide corpus plus prompting research, medium-high confidence]. The effective axis set from the grounding research: age (a specific number or tight band), face geometry (shape/jawline/cheekbones/chin/nose/forehead), eyes (color with modifier + shape + brow character), skin (tone + undertone in plain language), hair (the five-slot lock), build (somatotype-style words + a proportion-based height cue), and distinguishing marks (as test signal). Writing 'zygomatic width 142mm' wastes tokens the model cannot honor; writing 'high cheekbones' lands. Each axis gets its own node because each has its own failure mode; this node owns the shared principle — pick words from the categorical vocabulary a text encoder has strong visual priors for, and prefer one precise categorical term over three vague ones.

included: the categorical-not-metric granularity principle
the seven-axis inventory the bible draws from
prioritizing high-visual-prior words
excluded: per-axis word lists (their own nodes)
the reference conditioning that carries what text cannot (the carrier-division node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: run-phase per-term stability evidence or a model family with finer geometric control

pros.claim: Choosing categorical high-prior words concentrates the limited word budget on attributes the model can actually hold
pros.example: replacing a 30-word poetic face description with 'oval-square face, chiseled jawline, high cheekbones, straight nose' and getting more stable renders in fewer tokens

cons.claim: Categorical words are shared priors, so two personas built from nearby categories can render similar unless axes are deliberately differentiated
cons.example: giving both personas 'high cheekbones, almond eyes, olive skin' and finding solo shots of A and B blur toward one face family

failure_modes: writing metric geometry the encoder has no prior for
padding the block with vague adjectives ('beautiful', 'striking') that carry no categorical signal
building both personas from overlapping category choices
acceptance_tests: every bible line maps to one of the seven axes in categorical vocabulary, with no metric geometry and no signal-free adjectives

nodes.definition: Anchor age with a specific number or tight band: '34 years old' beats 'adult' or 'young man', because unanchored ages wobble plus-or-minus 5-10 years between generations [ESTIMATE — consistency-guide corpus, carried as the grounding file carries it]. Age wobble is a named item in the drift taxonomy — the persona reading 25 in one shot and 45 in the next is one of the most audience-visible drift modes, and it interacts with grooming (stubble adds years) and lighting (hard light ages a face). For this program: persona A is fixed at 34, persona B at 29 [ESTIMATE — authored proposals awaiting owner sign-off]. The number is written into the bible block verbatim and never rounded, banded or paraphrased ('mid-thirties' is a different token than '34 years old' and re-opens the wobble).

age as a drift-taxonomy item
the fixed proposed ages 34 and 29
excluded: grooming states that shift apparent age (the grooming node)
the QC pass that checks the age band (the QC node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: run-phase apparent-age QC statistics for the anchored numbers

pros.example: writing '34-year-old man' in every prompt instead of 'young businessman' and stopping the 25-to-45 apparent-age swing across a batch

cons.claim: A fixed number cannot fully override other age cues, so lighting and grooming can still drag apparent age off the anchor
cons.example: a hard-noir lighting setup rendering the 34-year-old as visibly older despite the anchored number

nodes.definition: Author the face-geometry descriptor set from the categorical vocabulary generators respect [ESTIMATE — guide-corpus synthesis, medium-high confidence]: face shape (oval / square / heart / oblong), jawline (chiseled, squared, soft), cheekbones (high, prominent, subtle), chin (cleft, pointed, rounded), nose (straight, aquiline, slightly upturned), forehead (high, average). Each persona picks exactly one value per axis and the choices are deliberately differentiated between A and B so the two faces occupy different category cells (A: oval-square face, chiseled jawline, high cheekbones, straight nose; B: heart-shaped face, defined cheekbones, softly pointed chin, straight elegant nose — authored [ESTIMATE] proposals). Two constraints ride along: the composite must pass the fictional-likeness audit (a stack of precise choices can converge on a recognizable person), and the text carries face geometry only as far as text can — the drift literature is explicit that face geometry wobbles under an unchanged description, which is why reference conditioning exists [FACT — drift literature, sources 12-14].

cons.claim: Text-side face geometry remains the weakest identity anchor — the same six choices still render as sibling-level variation without reference conditioning
cons.example: an unchanged face block producing visibly different jaw widths across a 20-image batch, exactly the wobble the drift literature describes

nodes.definition: Author the eye descriptor set: color WITH a modifier ('dark hazel', 'grey-blue') rather than a bare color word, plus shape (almond, hooded, deep-set, upturned), plus brow character (straight dark brows, softly arched) [ESTIMATE — guide-corpus synthesis carried at the grounding file's confidence]. Eye lines sit inside the bible block and obey the identical-phrasing rule — 'hazel' drifting to 'brown' in one prompt is a re-rolled attribute, not a synonym.

nodes.definition: Author skin as tone PLUS undertone in plain language ('warm olive', 'fair with cool undertone', 'sun-kissed light tan') — the grounding research carries the claim that undertone words survive lighting changes better than bare tone words as [ESTIMATE — practitioner logic, medium confidence], and this KB carries it at exactly that strength. The stakes are high because the drift literature's most dramatic failure is lighting-induced identity swap: a drastic lighting/color change can make the model produce 'a different face that still matches the prompt' (soft daylight vs neon is the cited example) [FACT — drift literature, sources 12-14]. Skin-tone shift across lighting setups is a named drift-taxonomy item. Proposals: A 'warm olive skin', B 'sun-kissed light-olive skin' [ESTIMATE — authored]. The QC consequence is written into the checklist: judge skin tone against the LIT scene — consistent with the scene's lighting, not with a different person.

nodes.definition: Lock hair as a five-slot specification that is never partially filled: length + texture + specific color + style/part side + finish ('collarbone-length, softly waved, dark espresso brown, centre-parted, natural sheen'). The grounding research states the four base slots — length, texture, specific color, style/part side — as the always-all-slots rule [ESTIMATE — guide corpus], and its continuity section extends the lock to five slots by adding finish [ESTIMATE — authored craft, high confidence]. Any dropped slot is silently re-sampled by the generator and reads as drift: hair part flipping sides and length jumps are named drift-taxonomy items, and the research's editorial judgment is that an Instagram audience tracks hair harder than jawlines [ESTIMATE — medium confidence]. Color words are specific ('dark espresso brown'), never class words ('brunette') — the identical-phrasing rule applies with full force because hair is the bible's most paraphrase-tempting line.

part-flip and length-jump as named drift items
specific color words over class words

cons.claim: The lock constrains scene realism — wind, water and motion physically move hair, which the lock alone cannot accommodate
cons.example: a yacht-deck shot where loose collarbone-length waves cannot stay 'centre-parted, natural sheen' and every frame fails a literal slot check

writing 'brunette' where the bible says 'dark espresso brown'

edges.why_related: maximally specific face composites improve consistency but can converge on a recognizable real person
edges.resolution_rule: the guardrail wins unconditionally: any composite flagged by the likeness audit is re-composited even at a consistency cost, and no descriptor is ever sourced from a specific real person

edges.why_related: a strong logline tempts teams to treat text as an identity anchor, which the carrier division explicitly denies it
edges.resolution_rule: the carrier division wins: reference conditioning is mandatory for every lead-persona frame regardless of how strong the text anchor feels; the logline is credited only with context steering

conflict_axes.name: verbatim_lock_vs_natural_variety
conflict_axes.description: The identical-phrasing rule demands the same words forever, while writers instinctively vary synonyms and editors want fresh copy; generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens, so variety re-rolls attributes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verbatim wins for every bible and logline line; variety lives only in scene/action language outside the identity text

conflict_axes.name: axis_completeness_vs_word_budget
conflict_axes.description: Fully specifying all seven axes plus wardrobe pushes the block past the 50-100 word band where parts get ignored, but trimming axes reopens per-shot gap-filling.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the band wins; face-critical axes stay, periphery compresses or moves to logline/modules/Elements

conflict_axes.name: descriptor_specificity_vs_likeness_safety
conflict_axes.description: More specific face composites hold identity better but can accidentally converge on a recognizable real person, which the fictionality guardrail prohibits.
poles: audited fictional distance from any real person
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the guardrail wins unconditionally; re-composite any flagged face even at a consistency cost

conflict_axes.name: text_anchor_vs_reference_conditioning
conflict_axes.description: The bible/logline is cheap and universal but cannot enforce face identity at the model level, while reference conditioning (Souls/Elements) carries the face at setup cost.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: references carry the face for every lead frame; text keeps its context-stabilizing job and always rides along

conflict_axes.name: marks_as_anchor_vs_marks_as_signal
conflict_axes.description: A named mole/freckle feels like an identity anchor but generators drop or migrate marks, so relying on it produces false accepts and false rejects.
poles: trust the mark as identity proof
use the mark only as a per-shot reject signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: test-signal framing wins: a bad mark fails the shot, a good mark proves nothing — the embedding check remains the identity backstop

conflict_axes.name: soul_fidelity_vs_element_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Souls are the surface's trained identity-faithful carrier but are locked to two models and one soul_id per generation; Elements are instant and multi-placeholder but their fidelity gap vs Souls is unmeasured.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Souls for solo hero stills on the Soul models; Elements for duo frames and every non-Soul model; the fidelity gap stays [UNKNOWN] until run-phase measurement

conflict_axes.name: pair_unit_vs_two_individuals
conflict_axes.description: Shooting the personas mostly as a pair builds the shared world but fuses them into a locked unit and doubles per-shot identity risk; solo-heavy coverage reads as two separate feeds.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: solo shots of each persona in every location with duo frames deliberate and minimal — the pair reads as two individuals with a shared world and identity risk halves

conflict_axes.name: hair_scene_physics_vs_slot_continuity
conflict_axes.description: Wind and water scenes physically move hair, colliding with a literal reading of the five-slot lock; fighting the generator to keep loose hair tidy fails, but free improvisation reads as drift.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pre-authorized named wind variants (bun/slick) reconcile both: the slot lock holds per named state, and the state switches with the scene card

conflict_axes.name: palette_coordination_vs_matching
conflict_axes.description: Duo frames tempt head-to-toe color matching for visual unity, but the genre grammar demands complementary palettes ('his navy, her ivory') and never identical colors head-to-toe.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: complementary wins: each persona stays inside their own palette and duo frames are checked complementary-not-matching

edge_cases.description: A prompt author paraphrases 'dark espresso brown hair' as 'brunette' and the generator re-rolls the hair attribute as a different visual token
edge_cases.trigger: any synonym substitution inside the bible or logline text
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce copy-paste of the canonical block; QC rejects frames whose prompts deviated from the versioned text

edge_cases.description: The character block is moved from prompt start to mid-prompt by a template refactor and its assigned weight silently changes
edge_cases.trigger: prompt template restructuring that shifts the block's token position
edge_cases.mitigation: lock the block at position zero in every template and diff-check templates against the fixed-token-position rule before batch runs

edge_cases.description: A batch is generated with a vague age class ('young man') and the persona's apparent age wobbles plus-or-minus 5-10 years across the batch
edge_cases.trigger: the anchored age number is dropped or banded in a prompt
edge_cases.mitigation: restore the verbatim integer age and QC apparent age against the anchor's band on every kept frame

edge_cases.description: B's beauty mark migrates from cheekbone to under-eye in an otherwise perfect frame, or disappears entirely across half a batch
edge_cases.trigger: generator mark drop/migration, a known frequent behavior
edge_cases.mitigation: fail the affected shots (test signal), do not conclude the pipeline is broken, and never accept a drifted face because its mark rendered correctly

edge_cases.description: A drastic lighting change (soft daylight to neon night) makes the model produce a different face that still matches the prompt text
edge_cases.trigger: large lighting/color register shifts between scenes, the drift literature's cited failure
edge_cases.mitigation: judge skin against the lit scene, run the embedding check as the identity backstop, and lean on undertone phrasing whose lighting-survival claim is itself only [ESTIMATE]

edge_cases.description: A duo shot is attempted with a soul_id expecting both personas to render, but one soul_id per generation means the second identity has no carrier
edge_cases.trigger: routing a two-persona frame through the Soul path
edge_cases.mitigation: route all duo frames through two character Elements (multi-placeholder) or a both-identities-verified start frame, per the live-surface constraint

edge_cases.description: A request arrives to make a persona evoke a specific real celebrity 'with the face turned away so it's fine'
edge_cases.trigger: any specific-real-person evocation request, face hidden or not
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse with the boundary named; the closed lane admits no hidden-face workaround and this KB carries no technique for it

edge_cases.description: The rendered persona sheet, though built from generic categorical descriptors, converges on a recognizable real individual
edge_cases.trigger: the likeness audit or an external reviewer flags a resemblance
edge_cases.mitigation: re-composite the flagged axes, re-render, re-audit, and version the change; consistency cost is accepted

edge_cases.description: The program starts with no calibrated embedding accept threshold because no published calibration exists for synthetic-persona QC
edge_cases.trigger: the first production batches arrive before any accept/reject history exists
edge_cases.mitigation: run fully human-gated at first, build the canonical embedding from the Soul-training set, and calibrate the reject threshold empirically on the first few dozen accepted/rejected shots — the [UNKNOWN] stays named until measured

edge_cases.description: A yacht/wind scene is prompted with B's loose soft-waves default and every frame fails the literal five-slot check as wind moves the hair
edge_cases.trigger: a wind/water scene shot against a loose-hair state
edge_cases.mitigation: switch the scene card to the pre-authorized wind variant (sleek low bun) instead of fighting the generator or failing the batch

edge_cases.description: A dual-Element duo frame holds B's identity but drifts A's, because reference strength is split across two subjects and the degradation magnitude is unmeasured
edge_cases.trigger: any two-Element prompt, until the run phase measures the split-reference effect
edge_cases.mitigation: QC both identities independently in every duo frame, keep duo exposure minimal via solo-shots-per-location, and log results to close the named [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Charter the likeness guardrail before any face work
workflow.description: Write the fictional-composite requirement, the closed-lane refusal, the composite audit and the brands-as-aesthetic-only rule as binding program policy
workflow.gate: the charter states all three rules and the audit procedure, and every later step cites it

workflow.action: Fix the bible block principle and its two hard rules
workflow.description: Adopt the ~50-100 word verbatim block with identical phrasing forever and fixed token position at prompt start, tagging the word band [ESTIMATE]
workflow.gate: both hard rules and the band are stated with their honesty tags

workflow.description: Fix the seven categorical axes and the coarse-not-metric granularity principle the bibles will draw from
workflow.gate: all seven axes are listed with categorical value sets and no metric geometry

workflow.action: Author the per-axis descriptor sets (face, eyes, skin, hair, build, marks, age)
workflow.description: Write the face six-axis values, eye color-with-modifier + shape + brows, tone-plus-undertone skin, the five-slot hair lock, somatotype build with height cues, one mark per persona as test signal, and the anchored ages
workflow.gate: every axis has exactly-one-value choices per persona and A/B differ on at least three face axes plus hair

workflow.description: Author 1-2 line loglines of high-visual-prior context words per persona, crediting them only with default-fill steering and author consistency
workflow.gate: loglines carry context words with visual priors and no pipeline step relies on them for face identity

workflow.action: Assemble the worked A and B bibles as owner proposals
workflow.description: Compose both blocks from the descriptor sets, verify the word band, run the likeness audit on rendered sheets, and flag both as [ESTIMATE] proposals pending sign-off
workflow.artifact: persona bible v0.9 proposals (A and B)
workflow.gate: both blocks pass band, axis-coverage, differentiation and likeness-audit checks and carry explicit sign-off status

workflow.action: Assign palettes and accessory continuity sets
workflow.description: Fix each persona's closed palette with metals/leathers and the one-watch/one-jewelry-set/one-bag-family continuity set, complementary-not-matching for duo frames
workflow.gate: every wardrobe/accessory descriptor names only in-palette values and duo coordination is complementary

workflow.action: Enumerate grooming and hair states with wind variants
workflow.description: Name each persona's finite grooming/hair states with allowed scenes, fixing one stubble decision for A and pre-authorizing wind variants
workflow.gate: every state is named with allowed scenes and each persona has a wind variant

workflow.action: Route identity carriers on the live surface
workflow.description: Plan soul_cast sheet -> curate 5-20 frames -> train one Soul per persona; create one character Element per persona; keep the bible text riding in every prompt; tag the Element-vs-Soul gap [UNKNOWN]
workflow.gate: every planned frame class names its carrier and all platform claims trace to the live-surface file

workflow.action: Define the duo staging grammar and its platform routing
workflow.description: Adopt the who-where + one-connection-point + shared-eyeline prompt grammar, offset blocking, minimal contact, solo-shots-per-location, and route all duo frames through dual Elements or verified start frames
workflow.gate: no duo frame routes through a Soul and every duo prompt satisfies the staging grammar

workflow.action: Stand up the persona QC gate and versioning loop
workflow.description: Install the per-batch human checklist plus embedding backstop with the calibrate-empirically mandate, and wire systematic failures into versioned bible revisions
workflow.gate: every kept frame has a checklist record, thresholds are marked calibrated-or-provisional, and failures route to versioned revisions

priority_rationale: The guardrail and block-format foundations come first because every descriptor choice is legal and mechanical only inside them; the descriptor-axis vocabulary and its seven per-axis sets come next because they are the raw material the bibles are assembled from; the worked A/B bibles, palettes, grooming canon and accessory sets then instantiate the system into two concrete owner-signable personas; the carrier division and duo routing follow because they bind the finished text artifacts to the live platform's Souls/Elements under the one-soul constraint; and the QC gate and versioning protocol come last because they observe production output and govern how everything upstream is allowed to change.

dominance_rules.rule: The likeness guardrail dominates every consistency or aesthetic gain
dominance_rules.rationale: a fictional program that evokes a specific real person — face shown or hidden — fails at the program level regardless of image quality
dominance_rules.trigger: a descriptor choice, reference image or request implicates a specific real person
dominance_rules.action: refuse the closed-lane request, re-composite any flagged face, and never source descriptors from a real individual

dominance_rules.rule: Verbatim bible text dominates prose elegance and editorial variety
dominance_rules.rationale: generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens, so any paraphrase re-rolls the attribute it touches
dominance_rules.trigger: anyone proposes to reword, translate or 'freshen' a bible or logline line
dominance_rules.action: keep the canonical text verbatim; route variety into scene/action language outside the identity block

dominance_rules.rule: Reference conditioning dominates text for face identity; text dominates references for context
dominance_rules.rationale: reference injection is the structural fix for drift that prompting cannot enforce, while the bible stabilizes wardrobe/age/grooming that references do not carry
dominance_rules.trigger: a lead-persona frame is planned, or someone proposes dropping the bible from a reference-conditioned prompt
dominance_rules.action: attach the persona's Soul/Element or verified start frame AND keep the verbatim bible text in the prompt

dominance_rules.rule: The live-surface enumeration dominates memory and marketing claims for platform capability
dominance_rules.rationale: model ids, soul/element constraints and media roles were read off the live MCP surface; anything else is unverified
dominance_rules.trigger: a routing or capability claim about Higgsfield is made
dominance_rules.action: quote higgsfield_surface.md; if the surface does not state it, tag it [UNKNOWN] rather than asserting it

dominance_rules.rule: The one-soul-per-generation constraint dominates duo ambitions
dominance_rules.rationale: the surface hard-limits Souls to one soul_id per generation and to the two Soul models, so no duo frame can be Soul-carried
dominance_rules.action: route through two character Elements in one prompt or a both-identities-verified start frame

dominance_rules.rule: Pre-authorized state variants dominate fighting the generator
dominance_rules.rationale: keeping loose hair tidy in wind scenes fails repeatedly, while a named wind variant preserves continuity as a deliberate state switch
dominance_rules.trigger: a scene's physics conflicts with a persona's default hair/grooming state
dominance_rules.action: switch the scene card to the pre-authorized variant instead of regenerating against physics

dominance_rules.rule: Versioned change dominates per-shot improvisation for any appearance evolution
dominance_rules.rationale: unversioned changes accumulate as drift and split the persona's identity across prompts, while versioned events keep evolution auditable
dominance_rules.trigger: any bible line, state list, palette or accessory is about to change
dominance_rules.action: record a version bump with owner approval and execute its invalidation list (references, embeddings) before the next batch

dominance_rules.rule: Owner sign-off dominates authored proposals for every appearance decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the worked bibles, palettes and grooming states are [ESTIMATE] proposals; appearance decisions belong to the owner and premature canonization forces expensive retraining
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal is about to be treated as canon (Soul training, mass generation)
dominance_rules.action: obtain explicit sign-off first, or clearly mark outputs as proposal renders

dominance_rules.rule: Coarse categorical descriptors dominate millimetre geometry in all identity text
dominance_rules.rationale: generators respond to high-signal categorical attributes and cannot honor metric geometry, which wastes the limited word budget
dominance_rules.trigger: a metric or over-precise descriptor is proposed for a bible
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the categorical vocabulary term and spend the saved words on an uncovered axis

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the fictional-likeness audit on rendered sheets BEFORE training Souls or creating Elements
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retraining every identity carrier and discarding curated sheets after a likeness flag on an already-productionized face

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get owner sign-off on both bible proposals BEFORE mass generation or Soul training
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating hundreds of frames and retraining references because a jawline or hair decision was never actually approved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the canonical bible text and its prompt-start position BEFORE the first production batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a batch split across paraphrased or repositioned blocks whose frames cannot be intermixed and must be reshot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the two personas' descriptor sets differentiated (three-plus face axes and hair) BEFORE rendering sheets
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at the duo stage that A and B blur together and re-authoring one persona from scratch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Curate the soul_cast persona sheet down to 5-20 approved frames BEFORE Soul training
anti_rework_rules.prevents: training a Soul on an uncurated sheet and baking a drifted or off-canon face into the program's strongest carrier

anti_rework_rules.rule: Create one character Element per persona up front, alongside the Souls
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stalling every duo frame and every non-Soul model at production time because the only carriers are Souls that cannot serve them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the canonical QC embedding from the Soul-training set BEFORE scoring any batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-scoring earlier batches against a late or drifting canonical embedding and re-litigating already-shipped accepts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name each persona's grooming states, one stubble decision and wind variants BEFORE shooting varied scenes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad-hoc per-scene grooming improvisations that read as drift and force reshoots once states are finally enumerated

iteration_protocol.trigger: owner sign-off or amendment lands on a bible, palette, grooming state or accessory proposal
iteration_protocol.action: bump the bible version, execute the invalidation list (retrain Souls/Elements and rebuild the canonical embedding for face-adjacent changes), and retire old-version prompts

iteration_protocol.trigger: the likeness audit or an external reviewer flags a persona as resembling a recognizable real individual
iteration_protocol.action: halt generation for that persona, re-composite the flagged face axes, re-render and re-audit the sheet, and version the change through the full invalidation list

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first few dozen accepted/rejected shots accumulate into a calibration set
iteration_protocol.action: calibrate the program's embedding reject threshold empirically, mark the QC gate calibrated, and record the threshold as deployment-specific

iteration_protocol.trigger: run-phase generations measure the Element-vs-Soul fidelity gap or dual-Element duo degradation
iteration_protocol.action: replace the named [UNKNOWN]s with measured values and re-balance the carrier routing (solo and duo) accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: QC batch statistics show a specific descriptor term or hair slot drifting repeatedly on the chosen models
iteration_protocol.action: swap the unstable term for a stabler categorical alternative, version the bible line, and re-verify on a test batch

iteration_protocol.trigger: the live Higgsfield surface changes Soul/Element constraints, compatible model lists or adds a new identity carrier
iteration_protocol.action: re-enumerate the surface, update the carrier division and duo routing to the fresh facts, and re-tag anything the new surface no longer states

iteration_protocol.trigger: video_analysis_create is tested for identity-similarity scoring in the feedback loop
iteration_protocol.action: resolve the [UNKNOWN] on its capability and, if it scores identity, wire it into the QC gate as an automated pre-filter

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new scene register appears that no named grooming state or staging convention covers
iteration_protocol.action: author the missing state or convention as a versioned addition with owner approval before shooting the register
